packs.title: Island in the Details
packs.promise: Move between island streets, architectural surprises and the shore.

q.s: Collect three kinds of edge on a large public-facing building.
st: Find a public-sidewalk view of the red-brick building without entering museum grounds.
Identify a curved opening, a straight brick edge and a recess holding shadow.
Make a three-edge card and explain which edge gives the building the most depth.

q.s: Write a tiny sequence that stays on land.
st: Choose a public path position away from water edges, play areas and event equipment.
Pick a near ground detail, a middle-distance park feature and a distant view.
Write three short frame descriptions that move from near to far, ending with one detail you would keep still.

q.s: Find three lines before your feet reach the beach.
st: Remain on an open landward path; no sand or water access is required.
Find a straight built edge, a softer planting edge and a distant waterline.
Describe which line feels nearest and which changes most as you look.

packs.title: Harbor at Human Scale
packs.promise: Read the Historic Seaport through small tools, changing uses and quiet observations.

q.s: Find three details that help a harbor function.
st: Choose a public promenade viewpoint outside restaurant seating and working docks.
Find a built edge, a way for people to move, and a feature that separates public space from boat operations.
Record a practical job for each detail; any three suitable features count.

q.s: Fit a broad view into a very small frame.
st: Stop where you can remain clear of pedestrians and restaurant tables.
Choose a close edge, a middle-distance shape and a patch of water or sky.
Draw a thumbnail no larger than your palm and give the composition a five-word title.

q.s: Find three different ways a line crosses a view.
st: Remain on the public Harborwalk outside marina gates.
Find a vertical, a diagonal and a curve among visible harbor structures, rigging or path edges.
Turn the three lines into a small alphabet of your own and explain one letter’s shape.
